messages:
kai (CSE): FYI - ACME reported 403s after SSO provisioning. They say embeddings work for other providers but with our SSO-created service key they're getting 403: "missing scope: embeddings" when calling /v1/embeddings and also 403 on /v1/generate. Customer says key came from our SCIM/sso provisioning flow (service account). Need repro steps and a quick mitigation.

zoe (CSE): Can you paste the exact curl they used and the full error body? Also which org/org-id and the service key id (svc_*) if they provided it?

kai (CSE): Sent what they pasted:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":"hello"}'
```

Response body: `{"error":{"code":403,"message":"insufficient_scope","details":"missing scope: embeddings"}}`

They also tried generation: 

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-3.5","input":"hi"}'
```

Response: `{"error":{"code":403,"message":"insufficient_scope","details":"missing scope: generation"}}`

zoe (CSE): OK. That smells like the SSO provisioning profile mapped to a reduced role (embeddings-only or empty). Liam / infra folks - can we check key metadata from the admin side? We need to confirm which scopes are attached to svc_abc123 and the provisioning profile mapping.

liam (eng): I can check. Running an internal lookup: `internal-admin keys inspect svc_abc123 --org acme-corp` (we also have an admin HTTP endpoint). Results: `{"id":"svc_abc123","org":"acme-corp","scopes":[],"created_by":"sso-provisioner","profile":"sso-embed-profile-v2"}`. So the key has no scopes.

sre-bot: authz: key=svc_abc123 check: embeddings -> DENY (missing); generation -> DENY (missing); rerank -> DENY (missing)

zoe (CSE): That matches customer experience. Repro steps for others to run locally:

1) Create a test SSO-provisioned service key (or use the one above if permitted).
2) Run the embeddings request as above.
3) Observe 403 with `insufficient_scope`.

liam (eng): Root cause hypothesis: SCIM/SAML provisioning mapping updated recently to support a narrower role; when the key was created the profile binding didn't carry the default scopes list. Two remediation options: (A) patch the key to add scopes, or (B) re-run provisioning so the correct scope list is applied on creation.

Quick fix (we can do this for the customer if ops approves):

PATCH via admin API:

```http
PATCH /internal/admin/v1/keys/svc_abc123
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "scopes": ["embeddings","generation","rerank"] }
```

After the patch the customer should be able to call both endpoints. Example verify step: run the same curl and expect 200 + embedding vector or generation token stream.

zoe (CSE): Customer asked if rotating the key is necessary. Answer: if the provisioning system will reassign proper scopes on rotation, rotating is a safe way to force the profile mapping to apply (but only if the provisioning mapping has been fixed). If not, rotation will produce another key without scopes. So either patch or fix mapping first.

kai (CSE): Customer also asked for a short-term workaround they can do on their side. We suggested creating a non-SSO service key via console (manual create) with the correct scopes and swapping it into their app until we fix the SSO flow. They prefer not to, so they'd rather we patch.

liam (eng): I'll prepare a one-time patch for svc_abc123 and follow up on the provisioning mapping. Action items:
- Patch key scopes for svc_abc123 (eng ops)
- Audit recent sso profiles created in last 90 days for empty/partial scopes (eng infra)
- Add unit test to provisioning service that validates scope lists are non-empty (eng)

sre-bot: action logged: PATCH-request queued for svc_abc123 by liam. Please include approval ticket ID.

zoe (CSE): I'll message the customer with the mitigation plan and timeline. Also asked them to provide the SDK stack they use (serverless, node sdk version) so we can confirm no caching issue with key config.

kai (CSE): Customer responded confirming svc_abc123 is the one created by their IdP team and gave their org id. They gave permission to proceed with the fix.

liam (eng): After patching, confirm with: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":"test"}' | jq
```
Expect a 200 and `data` array. Also check generation endpoint.

zoe (CSE): Follow-up note for the runbook we'll add: when an SSO-provisioned key gets 403s for both embeddings and generation, inspect `scopes` on the key object. If empty or missing required scope, either patch or rotate after fixing provisioning mapping. Include example admin PATCH and curl above.

kai (CSE): Thanks team. I'll update the ticket and add the customer-facing instructions. :thumbsup:

liam (eng): Patch done, verified 200 on embeddings. Closing loop once customer confirms in prod.

kai (CSE): Customer confirmed green in their staging and will roll to prod tomorrow. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
